title: Quibi (2018–2020): $1.75B for phone-only video · Spectre Brands
description: Quibi was a $1.75 billion streaming service of shows in ten-minute chapters, made for phones. It launched in April 2020 and announced its closure that October.

card.blurb: Hollywood’s studios and Wall Street put $1.75 billion into ten-minute shows for phones. The service launched into a lockdown, charged for what rivals gave away, and was gone in eight months.

hero.dates: Launched Apr 6, 2020. Announced its wind-down Oct 21, 2020. Dark by Dec 1, 2020.
hero.standfirst: The name meant “quick bites.” The company turned out to be one.
hero.deck: Quibi was a streaming service for premium shows in chapters of ten minutes or less, watchable only on a phone, and it announced its closure in October 2020, 198 days after launch. Jeffrey Katzenberg and Meg Whitman had raised $1.75 billion for it. The app arrived a few weeks into the pandemic lockdowns, could not be cast to a television or screenshotted, and cost $4.99 a month in a market full of free short video. The sources are the founders’ own letter, Roku’s filings, contemporary reporting and the archived website. Quibi was private, so most of its numbers are press reports or estimates, and are [labeled as such](/about/).
hero.artCaption: Original illustration: a phone turning between portrait and landscape, the feature Quibi called Turnstyle. Not an official Quibi asset.

findings.title: It charged for something the phone already gave away.
findings.text: Quibi cost $4.99 a month with ads or $7.99 without, against free short video on YouTube and TikTok. The founders’ own letter allowed that “the idea itself wasn’t strong enough to justify a standalone streaming service.”[^1][^10]

findings.title: Phone-only was a choice, and it was reversed too late.
findings.text: Whitman said the team considered television apps and decided against them. AirPlay arrived seven weeks after launch; the television apps arrived the day before the shutdown was announced.[^2][^10][^30]

findings.title: The pandemic hurt, but it helped everyone else.
findings.text: Katzenberg said “I attribute everything that has gone wrong to coronavirus.” In the same year Disney+ reached 73.7 million paid subscribers.[^5][^33]

findings.title: The plan needed scale immediately.
findings.text: The reported first-year target was 7.4 million paying subscribers. By June the Wall Street Journal reported the company was on course for fewer than 2 million and expected to need another $200M.[^7][^8]

findings.title: It stopped with money left.
findings.text: The founders closed the company rather than spend the remainder, and reportedly returned about $350M of the $1.75B. Roku bought the shows for a reported sum under $100M.[^2][^16]
